paragraphs: A helicopter crew helmet differs from a jet pilot's in ways that matter: no oxygen mask, a boom microphone instead, a dual visor housing on top and earcups sized for constant rotor noise rather than for cabin pressure. Those differences are what let a viewer place the wearer in the right kind of aircraft.

The mesh is light at 20,176 polygons and 20,942 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 7 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the shell finish, the strap webbing and the visor tint.

At $49 it suits military aviation visualisation, film and television costume, character set dressing for games, equipment presentation and training material. On sale since 2017, kept to real-world scale so it fits a standard head.

A period infantry pack is a simple thing carried badly: a canvas or tarred cloth knapsack with a rolled blanket strapped over the top, worn until the straps stretch and the corners go soft. That wear is the whole character, because a crisp new pack looks like a reenactment prop rather than something carried on a march.
The mesh is light at 7,392 polygons and 7,801 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the blanket roll and the strap arrangement.

At $49 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits historical film and television, museum and heritage material, reenactment reference, education content, character set dressing and games. On sale since 2025.

A Victorian fireplace is an assembly rather than an opening: a cast iron insert with a decorated surround, a tiled slip either side, a hearth in front and a mantel above. Including a fire changes what the object communicates entirely - an empty grate reads as architecture, a lit one reads as a room in use.
The mesh runs 51,398 polygons and 52,946 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the cast iron ornament and the tile detail where a close camera lands.

At $49 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits period interior visualisation, heritage property marketing, film and television set dressing, hospitality and residential renders, and games. On sale since 2025.

A chase tag arena is a parkour course built to a fixed footprint: a symmetrical grid of walls, blocks, bars and vaults arranged so two athletes can run it in either direction. The symmetry matters competitively, and it makes the structure look engineered rather than like a playground.
The mesh runs 259,875 polygons and 278,252 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry spread across every obstacle in the course.
At $49 and built to StemCell specification, it suits sports broadcast graphics, competition and event visualisation, parkour and fitness material, sports advertising and games. On sale since 2025.

Runway lighting is a set rather than a single fitting: threshold lights, edge lights, centreline units and the navigation lamps that mark the approach, each with its own colour and mounting. Supplying them together is what lets a runway be laid out correctly rather than repeating one fixture the whole length.
The mesh is 64,322 polygons and 64,840 vertices, built entirely from quads with mixed UV layout. All-quad geometry subdivides cleanly, which is useful on fittings that sometimes need to fill a frame.

At $44 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits airport and airfield visualisation, aviation infrastructure presentation, night approach scenes, simulator projects and games. On sale since 2026.

Solar powered airfield lighting is a different product from mains fitted units: each lamp carries its own panel and battery, so there are no cables to trench and the fittings can be deployed on unprepared strips. That self-contained construction gives them a taller profile with the panel on top, which is the identifying feature.
The mesh runs 92,580 polygons and 46,785 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the lamp head, the solar panel and the ground base.

At $44 it suits airfield and aviation infrastructure visualisation, remote and temporary airstrip presentation, equipment marketing, humanitarian and military aviation material, and games. On sale since 2023.

Flight deck crew helmets carry a communications set and a colour code. The colour identifies the job - fuel, ordnance, catapult, handling - and the mic and receiver are essential because nobody can hear anything on a deck with engines running. The cranial style shell wraps the head rather than sitting on it.

The mesh is light at 11,090 polygons and 11,244 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a symmetrical shell with paired earcups, and the StemCell build means it works in a real-time engine.

At $44 it suits naval and carrier operations visualisation, aviation ground crew material, industrial safety presentation, film and television, and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard head. On sale since 2026.

A jet pilot's helmet is a mounting platform. The shell carries a visor track, an oxygen mask bayonet on each side, a communications lead and increasingly a mount for a display or night vision. Those attachment points are what make it read as fast jet equipment rather than as a generic flight helmet.
The mesh runs 54,763 polygons and 57,473 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the visor mechanism, the bayonet receivers and the shell edge.

At $44 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits military aviation visualisation, film and television costume, character set dressing for games, equipment marketing and training material. Real-world scale is kept. On sale since 2025.

This is a bust rather than a full figure, and at enormous scale: a face and matted hair rising from the ground, eyes closed in meditation, with no body below. That truncation is the design, and it gives the sculpture a presence quite unlike a conventional standing statue.
The mesh is light at 13,262 polygons and 6,685 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a subject read at distance from silhouette and surface rather than from fine detail.

At $39 and built to StemCell specification, it suits travel and tourism material, cultural and religious visualisation, landmark and city renders, documentary work, education and games. On sale since 2023.

A unit load device is shaped by the aircraft it fits. The lower hold of a widebody is a circular cross section, so the container has one angled lower corner to match the curve of the fuselage. That single cut corner is what identifies a ULD instantly and what a rectangular box gets wrong.
The mesh is efficient at 67,234 polygons and 35,119 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the corner profile, the door and the base rails.

A white version sits on this page at the same $39. Both suit airport cargo and ground handling visualisation, air freight and logistics presentation, apron scenes, supply chain material and games. On sale since 2023.

An ammunition crate is a stencilled wooden or steel box with rope handles at the ends, latches on the lid and a gasket around the rim. The stencilling is the informative part: lot numbers, calibre and hazard markings, all applied in a standard format that makes the box readable to anyone in a supply chain.

The mesh runs 127,321 polygons and 128,469 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 14 texture maps at 2048x2048 carrying the stencils, the paint and the wear at the corners.

A green version sits on this page at the same $39. Both suit military and defence visualisation, film and television set dressing, warehouse and depot scenes, historical material and games. On sale since 2016.

This missile is fired from a tripod or a vehicle mount and guided by a laser beam the operator keeps on the target. The round itself is a sealed tube with a tandem warhead, which is why the nose has a small probe standing ahead of the main charge: the first charge defeats reactive armour, the second does the work.
The mesh is light at 19,568 polygons and 9,971 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a weapon usually shown as one of several rounds beside a launcher.

At $39 it suits defence and conflict visualisation, news and documentary graphics, military training material, analysis content and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it seats correctly in a launcher. On sale since 2023.

A plastic bodied shopping trolley is a European supermarket fixture: a moulded basket rather than a wire one, on a steel frame with four castors and a child seat that folds down. The moulded body is quieter, does not rust and takes branding directly, which is why it has largely replaced wire in food retail.
The mesh runs 68,288 polygons and 69,263 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 5 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the moulded plastic finish and the frame paint.

At $39 and built to StemCell specification, it suits supermarket and retail interior visualisation, store planning presentation, retail marketing, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2020.

An aircraft autocannon is a very long thin weapon dominated by its barrel, because muzzle velocity matters more than anything else and length buys it. Around the breech sits the recoil mechanism, the feed and the mounting lugs, and the whole assembly is built to be bolted into an airframe rather than handled.
The mesh runs 111,828 polygons and 55,962 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the breech, the feed mechanism and the mounting hardware.
At $39 and built to StemCell specification, it suits military aviation visualisation, aircraft cutaways and technical material, defence presentation, documentary work and games. On sale since 2024.
